question: Across dozens of studies of athletes, how much of the difference in skill did hours of deliberate practice explain?
answer: About a fifth. Macnamara, Moreau and Hambrick pooled the sports studies and found deliberate practice accounted for 18% of the variation in performance. Among elite athletes alone it explained just 1%: at the top everyone practises hard, so hours stop telling them apart.
move: When everyone puts in the work, the work stops explaining who wins.
ask: Where am I assuming more hours will close a gap that hours alone may not explain?
trap: Trusting the popular story that practice hours explain nearly everything.
source: Macnamara, Moreau & Hambrick, Perspect Psychol Sci, 2016
reference: Macnamara, Moreau & Hambrick, The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports: A Meta-Analysis, Perspectives on Psychological Science, 2016
